_comment: GLM dev-drainer settings (issue #3688, ADR-0032 invariant 8, input-side half of the two-layer secret fence). Handed to the drainer's `claude` process via `--settings` by src/glm/drainer-runner.ts buildDrainerArgs(). The `deny` block is the load-bearing part: z.ai offers no training opt-out (ADR-0032 accepted risk), so credential material must never enter the drainer's context in the first place. Claude Code evaluates deny BEFORE allow, so the broad `allow` tool grants below cannot re-open a denied path. Deliberately NOT run under --dangerously-skip-permissions: an explicit allow list plus a deny fence keeps the precedence unambiguous. Note the Bash denials are prefix-matched and therefore defense-in-depth, not a hard sandbox — the Read denials are the real fence.
